## Motivation and scope

Add Ascend deployment recipes and measured results to the Qwen3 cookbook. Related task: https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/1216.

Following the explicit hardware and validation boundaries in merged PR #40120, this contribution reports A3 measurements for 8B/30B and A2 measurements for 32B/235B. Multi-card A3 resources were unavailable; A2 results do not establish A3 performance equivalence. This documentation stage does not close the full hardware-validation task.

## Changes

- Add seven single-node, PD co-located recipes, with editable model paths, interfaces, service settings, and reproduction commands. Physical cards and logical NPU devices are labelled separately.
- Record complete accuracy and performance measurements for six recipes: A3 8B TP1/TP2, A3 30B low-latency/high-throughput, and A2 32B BF16/W8A8.
- Record A2 eight-device 235B W8A8 startup and 200-question GSM8K accuracy, while retaining its unverified status because the performance workload did not complete. The subset has its own accuracy label, with no fabricated speed metrics.
- Retain historical GPQA context-limit failures separately from the corrected 38000-token reruns. No answers or scores are spliced across attempts.
- Add six command-generator regression tests under docs/scripts/tests/, covering logical device counts, draft requirements, editable paths containing spaces, partial verification, stale selections, and the unchanged GPU default. The cookbook CI step executes that test directory, matching the convention accepted in #40120.

## Accuracy evidence

| Actual hardware / recipe | Protocol | Correct / scored | Result | Successful requests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 8B W8A8 TP2 | GSM8K, 5-shot, temperature 0, output 512 | 1157/1314 | 88.05% | 1314/1314 |
| A3 8B W8A8 TP1 | GPQA Diamond, temperature 1, output 38000 | 112/198 | 56.57% | 198/198 |
| A3 30B-A3B W8A8 TP2 | AIME 2025, temperature 1, output 32768 | 23/30 | 76.67% | 30/30 |
| A2 32B BF16 TP4 | GSM8K, 5-shot, temperature 0, output 512 | 1139/1314 | 86.68% | 1314/1314 |
| A2 32B W8A8 TP4 | GPQA Diamond, temperature 1, output 38000 | 132/198 | 66.67% | 198/198 |
| A2 235B W8A8 TP8 | GSM8K fixed 200-question subset, 5-shot, temperature 0, output 512 | 192/200 | 96.0% | 200/200 |

The two 30B workload recipes share one accuracy run. The 32B BF16 result includes all 178 output-budget stops; AIME includes all three output-budget stops. The corrected A3 8B TP1 and A2 32B GPQA runs both completed with 198 natural stops. Historical 40000-token attempts are retained with the context-limit rejection included in the denominator; they do not validate the revised protocol.

The 235B run uses dataset rows 0–4 as demonstrations and rows 5–204 for evaluation, plain completion prompts without a chat template, top-p 1, 128 client threads, and a server limit of eight requests. All 200 responses finished with stop, with no recorded API errors or missing responses. Independent rescoring agrees. This is neither full GSM8K nor the registered A3 test, and it does not validate the A3 TP16/DP16 reference.

## Performance evidence and remaining work

| Recipe | TP | Concurrency | Successful requests | Mean TTFT ms | Mean TPOT ms | Service output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 8B low latency | 2 | 1 | 4/4 | 920.20 | 4.11 | 211.62 |
| A3 8B high throughput | 1 | 64 | 256/256 | 4578.23 | 29.94 | 1778.40 |
| A3 30B low latency | 2 | 1 | 1/1 | 169.15 | 5.57 | 175.69 |
| A3 30B high throughput | 2 | 160 | 640/640 | 3619.48 | 46.05 | 3026.47 |
| A2 32B BF16 | 4 | 1 | 4/4 | 2888.82 | 32.96 | 29.69 |
| A2 32B W8A8 | 4 | 100 | 400/400 | 7326.95 | 73.59 | 1068.48 |

These are individual complete runs, not repeated-run confidence intervals. The one-request 30B low-latency result is not a latency distribution. Workload lengths, runtime, and reproduction commands are documented on the page.

The 235B performance workload planned 32 requests at 3500 input / 1500 output tokens and concurrency 8, with a separate warmup. It exited with timeout code 124 after 900 seconds; the last progress log was 1/32 and no final metrics were generated. No performance score is reported, including from the accuracy evaluator or instantaneous server throughput. A complete independent performance run remains follow-up work. BF16 235B is not offered as a tested recipe and remains deferred pending storage and compute resources.

## Reproducibility and validation

A3 measurements use c389dd086340878934bf96bc209534f1fbb8440c. A3 performance is from September 12; the new TP1 accuracy run is from October 21 and is labelled separately. A2 32B and 235B use b44e2486824e2fbde9cbcb09adad10bce5593c16. Runtime versions and checkpoint sources are recorded in the documentation.

For 235B, ModelScope revision aa1470b37a666db251ef9bbc76256fa611a1d87c of vllm-ascend/Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8 comprises 66 files / 236803017357 bytes, all SHA256-verified. All 107 exported evidence files were verified; the archive SHA256 is c0082d5fff5ee03346baaedf6911a97b6c53765a8fb1263d7d47cc13bc4b4fc6. The final process/NPU checks were clear and the environment was shut down. The A3 TP1 retest has 42 exported, hash-verified evidence files.

Latest reviewed head: `4feaf6e3a4b5e80d7a0ef461143f1424df73af0a`, which merges main and resolves the lint workflow conflict.

- [GitHub Lint passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41399848824), including pre-commit, cookbook authoring contracts and command tests, PR title tests, offline documentation references, and Mintlify broken-links.
- [Base CI passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41399848886). Workflow success does not imply that skipped device tests ran.
- [Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41399848936/job/125129230354) and [AMD Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41399848782/job/125129094120) stopped at the missing `run-ci` label before runtime tests. Their gates also require `run-ci-nv-extra` and `run-ci-amd-extra`, respectively. Maintainers can decide whether these additional suites are needed.
- After the merge, all 58 local cookbook tests and 99 PR title tests passed, along with the change whitespace check. Earlier Mintlify build validation and independent review of the numerical evidence remain recorded; model measurements were not rerun for this merge.
- The earlier Windows launcher/link-check limitations were local tooling issues; the corresponding checks now pass in GitHub Lint. A fresh local visual preview was not completed. [Mintlify fork preview approval](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40677/checks?check_run_id=125129080187) is pending for this head.

This PR is ready for maintainer review of the documented A3/A2 results and bounded validation scope. The 235B W8A8 performance run remains incomplete, and 235B BF16 remains deferred. No unrun or skipped device/CI test is claimed as passed.

files.patch:
@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 ---
 title: Qwen3
+description: "Deploy Qwen3 with SGLang, including measured Ascend A3 and A2 recipes and their validation scope."
 metatags:
     description: "Deploy Qwen3 series models with SGLang - featuring advanced reasoning, 256K context, and flexible Dense/MoE architectures for edge to cloud."
 ---
@@ -54,6 +55,364 @@ import { Qwen3Deployment } from "/src/snippets/autoregressive/qwen3-deployment.j
   - `--speculative-draft-model-path`: The path of the draft model weights. This can be a local folder or a Hugging Face repo ID such as [`lmsys/SGLang-EAGLE3-Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-SpecForge-Meituan`](https://huggingface.co/lmsys/SGLang-EAGLE3-Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-SpecForge-Meituan).
 - **Xeon CPU service configuration:** Please refer to the `Notes` part in the serving engine launching section in [the SGLang CPU server document](../../../docs/hardware-platforms/cpu_server#launch-of-the-serving-engine) to better understand how to configure the arguments, especially for TP (tensor parallel) and NUMA binding settings.
 
+### 3.3 Ascend NPU deployment
+
+Use the selector below for **single-node, PD co-located** deployment: the same
+SGLang service handles prefill and decode. Select **A3** for the measured 8B and
+30B-A3B recipes, or **A2** for 32B recipes and the partially validated 235B-A22B recipe.
+Then select the model, quantization, and workload.
+
+An A3 physical card contains two 64 GB dies; an A2 card has one 64 GB device.
+Tensor parallelism counts logical devices: TP4 requires four A2 cards or two A3
+cards. The selector shows the card and device requirements for each recipe.
+See the [Ascend hardware reference](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/reference/glossary#hardware).
+
+| Model | Quantization | Workload | Hardware / physical cards | Logical devices / TP | Status |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Qwen3-8B | W8A8 | Low latency | A3 / 1 | 2 | Measured |
+| Qwen3-8B | W8A8 | High throughput | A3 / 1 allocated | 1 | Measured; GPQA retest 112/198 (56.57%) |
+| Qwen3-30B-A3B | W8A8 | Low latency / high throughput | A3 / 1 | 2 | Measured |
+| Qwen3-32B | BF16 | Low latency | A2 / 4 | 4 | Measured |
+| Qwen3-32B | W8A8 | High throughput | A2 / 4 | 4 | Measured |
+| Qwen3-235B-A22B | W8A8 | High throughput | A2 / 8 | 8 | Startup and GSM8K measured; performance incomplete |
+
+The 32B W8A8 recipe follows the command in the
+[A2 best practice](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_32b#qwen3-32b-w8a8-2p-in3k5-out1k5-55ms-a2-series).
+That source labels the scenario as two cards but launches with `--tp-size 4`.
+This selector explicitly requires four A2 devices to match the command.
+
+The measured 32B BF16 recipe uses TP4, up to eight concurrent requests, chunked prefill,
+and decode graph capture for batch sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8. Its low-latency
+performance workload uses client concurrency 1; GSM8K uses client concurrency 8.
+The 235B W8A8 candidate uses the tutorial's recommended TP8 with eight concurrent
+requests. Both start without EAGLE3; the 235B candidate disables graph capture and uses
+pure tensor parallelism. The A2 recipes do not inherit the A3 reference's TP16,
+DP16, fused MoE settings, or latency
+targets. The 32B W8A8 recipe passed startup, temperature-0/1 inference,
+its complete performance workload, and full GPQA evaluation with the corrected
+output budget. The 32B BF16
+recipe passed startup, temperature-0/1 inference, performance, and full GSM8K
+evaluation. The 235B W8A8 recipe passed model loading, service health, first
+inference, and the 200-question GSM8K evaluation described below. Its performance
+workload timed out and remains incomplete; this does not validate the A3 TP16/DP16 recipe.
+
+<Info>
+The [235B model tutorial](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_235b_a22b#model-weights)
+recommends 16 × 64 GB devices for BF16. On eight-device A2 nodes, matching
+that device count requires two nodes. That deployment
+needs a separate distributed configuration and validation of communication
+between the nodes. It remains pending and is not offered by this single-node
+selector. Its approximately 470 GB checkpoint also exceeds a 300 GB local volume;
+prepare sufficient shared storage before starting an instance.
+</Info>
+
+<Note>
+The 8B throughput reference uses TP=1, which uses one die of an A3 card. Preserve
+that topology when reproducing its benchmark. Changing the device count, draft
+model, or workload requires a new performance measurement.
+</Note>
+
+#### Prepare the environment and weights
+
+Complete [SGLang installation with NPU support](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation)
+and check `npu-smi info` before launching a recipe. These commands target SGLang
+**main**. Use the dependency combination documented for your CANN version and
+record the exact SGLang commit and runtime versions used for your run. The linked
+Ascend tutorials describe v0.5.16; earlier releases can use different flags.
+
+The A3 measurements and A2 32B validation use the following environments:
+
+| Component | A3, 2026-09-12 | A2 32B, 2026-09-22–23 |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| SGLang | `main` at `c389dd086340878934bf96bc209534f1fbb8440c` | `main` at `b44e2486824e2fbde9cbcb09adad10bce5593c16` |
+| CANN | `9.0.0` | `9.0.0` |
+| PyTorch / torch-npu | `2.10.0+cpu` / `2.10.0` | `2.10.0+cpu` / `2.10.0` |
+| sgl-kernel-npu | `2026.9.0` | `2026.9.0`, 910B / aarch64 package |
+| triton-ascend | `3.2.1.dev20260530` | `3.2.1.dev20260530` |
+| Transformers | `5.8.1` | `5.12.1` |
+
+The 2026-10-21 A3 8B TP1 GPQA retest used the same versions listed in the A3
+column, with Python 3.11.15, `memfabric-hybrid 1.0.8`, and `memfabric-zbal 1.1.1`.
+Its accuracy result is separate from the 2026-09-12 performance measurement.
+
+This records the tested platform environment. For a new installation, follow the
+linked dependency matrix and record any differences. EAGLE3 sampling at the A3
+measured commit requires `sgl_kernel_npu.sample.chain_speculative_sampling_triton`; the
+platform's older `2026.5.1` kernel failed on nonzero-temperature requests. The
+tested `2026.9.0` kernel provides that function.
+
+The A2 32B environment has four Ascend 910B3 devices and uses `memfabric-hybrid 1.1.4`
+and `memfabric-zbal 1.1.2`. Install the CANN 9.0.0 / 910B custom-ops,
+ops-transformer, and kernel packages from the [matching official release](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/releases/tag/2026.9.0). The A2
+measurements use the selected recipe without additional host tuning; they do
+not establish a controlled speedup over the published reference.
+
+Download the main checkpoint before starting the service. For recipes that enable
+EAGLE3, also download the matching **EAGLE3 draft**. The following tutorials provide
+weight sources and environment setup; select the **A2 / 910B** environment for A2
+hardware and the **A3** environment for A3 hardware:
+
+- [Qwen3-8B](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_8b#model-weights)
+- [Qwen3-30B-A3B](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_30b_a3b#model-weights)
+- [Qwen3-32B](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_32b#model-weights)
+- [Qwen3-235B-A22B](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_235b_a22b#model-weights)
+
+For W8A8, use a ModelSlim checkpoint with its quantization metadata. When EAGLE3
+is enabled, keep the draft unquantized as specified by the recipe. Original Qwen3, Instruct-2507, and
+Thinking-2507 checkpoints require compatible drafts; record both checkpoint
+revisions when testing a pair.
+
+The A2 32B assets are pinned to these **ModelScope** repository revisions. Their
+complete file manifests were checked against the downloaded sizes and SHA256
+digests; these revision identifiers refer to ModelScope, not Hugging Face.
+
+| ModelScope checkpoint | Revision |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `vllm-ascend/Qwen3-32B-W8A8` | `9ecdf711a9629fbf2385b17b47359c8a604e39ed` |
+| `Zjcxy-SmartAI/Eagle3-Qwen3-32B-zh` | `d7272a49b25d36d75f7ec629503fb704f67268db` |
+| `Qwen/Qwen3-32B` | `d64d397e66908737784bb9172614b88e085b2ad1` |
+
+In the NPU container, load the environment scripts supplied by your installation:
